name: Fly River Grassbird
rangeDescription: Southeastern new guinea (fly river lowlands)
description: A fairly small bird of marshes in the Trans-Fly of New Guinea. Best seen by boat.

name: Restinga Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Coastal southeastern brazil (southeastern são paulo to northeastern santa catarina)
description: Small olive-green flycatcher with a long slender tail that is often held cocked. Note the yellow eyebrow, yellow throat, and two wingbars.

name: Banded Antbird
rangeDescription: Southeastern colombia to eastern peru, northwestern bolivia, and northwestern and southern amazonian brazil
description: Chunky, short-tailed antbird of mature rainforest understory. Gets its name from its two broad cream wingbars, which give it a banded appearance.

name: Brown-cheeked Hornbill
rangeDescription: Humid forest of sierra leone to ghana
description: Big, spectacular black-and-white hornbill. Males have a large cream-colored bill, and females a much smaller and darker one.

name: Malaita Monarch
rangeDescription: Malaita (central solomon islands)
description: A small black-and-white monarch. White below except for black throat and breast.

name: Bearded Barbet
rangeDescription: Western sahel (northern senegambia to northwestern central african republic)
description: Large, colorful barbet with a huge ivory-colored bill. Note the red underparts with a thick black bar across the middle.

name: Mangrove Swallow
rangeDescription: Lowlands of northern mexico to panama
description: Small swallow of tropical lowlands. Usually near water, from mangroves and coastal lagoons to rivers well inland; mainly in small groups, often mixed with other species of swallows.

name: Slaty-breasted Wood-Rail
rangeDescription: Forest of southeastern brazil to paraguay and northeastern argentina (misiones)
description: Noisy and occasionally conspicuous inhabitant of marshy areas in and around forests. Gleaming red eye and legs.

name: Leymebamba Antpitta
rangeDescription: Local on west slope of the andes of western ecuador and northwestern peru (piura); east slope of the andes from northern peru (amazonas south of the río marañón) to northern bolivia (la paz)
description: Small antpitta found in montane forest in the Andes from northern Ecuador to Bolivia. Typical antpitta shape: plump with short tail and long legs.

name: Bolivian Warbling Finch
rangeDescription: Andes of bolivia and adjacent northwestern argentina (jujuy)
description: Striking tanager of open woodland and scrub in high elevations of the east slope of the Andes in central and southern Bolivia and extreme NW Argentina; including agricultural lands, and open Polylepis woodland. From Black-and-chestnut Warbling-Finch by white throat and paler underparts in Bolivian.

name: Japanese Waxwing
rangeDescription: Southeastern siberia and northern manchuria; winters to southern china and ryukyu islands (southern japan)
description: The only waxwing endemic to the old world, this species is similar to its Bohemian relative, but with pink instead of yellow tail tips and a yellow-tinged belly. Irruptive and inconsistent in its movements during the colder months, following crops of berries to wintering grounds, where it frequently gathers in large and noisy feeding flocks.

name: Greater Yellow-Finch
rangeDescription: Andes of northern and central chile and adjacent argentina
description: Fairly common in the Andes of central Chile and adjacent Argentina; seen readily at ski resorts, around villages, on bogs, and on stony and grassy slopes. Often in flocks, associates readily with other seed-eating birds.

name: Red-legged Seriema
rangeDescription: Central and eastern brazil to bolivia, paraguay, and central argentina
description: Unmistakable large terrestrial raptorial bird. Sandy-colored overall with very long red legs, a long tail, and tufty crest in front of the eyes.

name: Western Tragopan
rangeDescription: Himalayas of northern pakistan to northwestern india and adjacent southwestern tibet
description: A large, short-tailed pheasant. Male appears mostly dark with prominent white dots all over.

name: Pink-throated Brilliant
rangeDescription: Lower east slope of the andes from southern colombia to northern peru
description: Scarce hummingbird found in cloud forest in the eastern foothills of the Andes in Ecuador, southern Colombia, and northern Peru. Green with a white vent and a small white dot behind eye.

name: Peruvian Martin
rangeDescription: Coastal peru (piura southward to ica), rarely to northern chile (arica)
description: Scarce, local, and poorly known large swallow of lowland deserts and coastal areas. Usually seen as singles or small groups, usually apart from other swallows.

name: Brown Emutail
rangeDescription: Humid rainforest of eastern madagascar
description: Medium-sized, rich-brown bird with a weird spiky tail. Scarce and incredibly shy bird that is unlikely to be seen unless you’re expressly searching for it.

name: Crimson-backed Flameback
rangeDescription: Sri lanka
description: Large, spectacular woodpecker with crimson upperparts, black-scaled pale underparts, and a crested head. Males have a red crest, females a black crest with fine white markings.

name: Tufted Coquette
rangeDescription: Eastern venezuela, trinidad, and the guianas to northern brazil
description: Tiny, ornately patterned hummingbird with a bold pale rump band. Exquisite adult male plumage features a bushy orange crest and long orange plumes tipped dark green, sweeping back from the cheeks over the shoulders, and set off by a white rump band and stout orange bill tipped black.

name: Sichuan Bush Warbler
rangeDescription: Breeds in southern china (shaanxi, sichuan, guizhou, hubei, northwestern hunan, and northwestern jiangxi); nonbreeding range unknown
description: Drab brown warbler of hilly central China; russet-brown above and cold gray-brown below, with dark stripes on the vent. Like many other bush warblers, very difficult to see as it skulks deep in dense vegetation; typically prefers to scurry or run instead of fly to reach cover.
